# Badge: `jl-badge`

A short status, coloured by its tone.

- Class `JlBadge`, an atom: `import { JlBadge } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/badge

Badges label a state in a word or two. Keep the accent for what is live or waits for someone, and the
semantic tones for what they mean: ok for done, warn for a real warning, danger for a failure.

## Use

```ts
import { JlBadge } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlBadge dot label="Running" tone="accent" />
```

```html
<jl-badge dot label="Running" tone="accent"></jl-badge>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The text.
- `tone` (attribute `tone`): `'neutral' | 'accent' | 'ok' | 'warn' | 'danger' | 'info'`, default `'neutral'`. The colour, by meaning.
- `dot` (attribute `dot`): `boolean`, default `false`. A dot before the label, for live states.
- `icon` (attribute `icon`): `string`, default `''`. An icon before the label; it replaces the dot.
- `solid` (attribute `solid`): `boolean`, default `false`. Filled with the tone, for what must stand out.
- `hint` (attribute `hint`): `string`, default `''`. What the state means, as a tooltip: "Waiting for logistics to prepare it."

## Slots

- The default slot: Extra content after the label.

## Methods

- `showStatus(look: StatusLook): void`: Shows a state as an app's map of states describes it: its label, tone, icon and hint.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The pill.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Tones

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-badge label="Draft"></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="accent" label="In review"></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="ok" label="Published"></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="warn" label="Expiring"></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="danger" label="Failed"></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="info" label="New"></jl-badge>
</div>
```

### Dot and icon

A dot marks a live state; an icon says the state at a glance.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-badge tone="accent" label="Running" dot></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="ok" label="Online" dot></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="ok" icon="check" label="Verified"></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="danger" icon="circle-x" label="3 errors"></jl-badge>
</div>
```

### Solid

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-badge tone="neutral" label="v0.1" solid></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="accent" label="Beta" solid></jl-badge>
  <jl-badge tone="danger" label="12" solid></jl-badge>
</div>
```

### States from a map

One map per kind of thing gives each state its word, tone, icon and hint; showStatus() takes one. Hover a badge for its hint.

```html
<div class="row demo-statuses"></div>
```

```js
const ORDER_STATUS = {
  submitted: { label: 'Sent', tone: 'info', icon: 'inbox', hint: 'Waiting for logistics to prepare it.' },
  ready: { label: 'Ready', tone: 'ok', icon: 'check', hint: 'Ready to be handed over.' },
  cancelled: { label: 'Cancelled', tone: 'neutral', icon: 'x', hint: 'Cancelled before it was handed over.' },
};
for (const look of Object.values(ORDER_STATUS)) {
  const badge = new JlBadge();
  badge.showStatus(look);
  root.querySelector('.demo-statuses').append(badge);
}
```
